name: Split pea segment

cells.description: Interior cells, excluding both bounding circles.

definition: The interior digit sum equals either decimal concatenation of the two bounding circle digits. No distinctness condition is added.
example: Satisfies: circle digits 3,1 and interior 3,4,6 total 13. Breaks: the same circles and interior 3,4,5 total 12.

name: Split pea

cells.description: Interior positions of one line between two circles.

ends.description: The two circles, in either orientation.

definition: Interior digits sum to the two-digit decimal number made from the endpoints in either order.
example: Satisfies: interior 3,4,6 and endpoints 3,1 give sum 13. Breaks: interior 3,4,5 gives 12, neither 13 nor 31.

name: Japanese sums

strips.description: All rows from left and columns from top, including empty clue lists.

clues.description: Ordered runs for each strip; colours 1 blue, 2 purple, 3 orange; omitted total is ?. No unlisted runs.

definition: Choose one global colour per cell (0 unshaded, 1 blue, 2 purple, 3 orange). Each strip has exactly the listed nonempty maximal runs in clue order. A run has its clue colour and known digit sum. Runs of the same colour need at least one unshaded cell between; differing colours can touch. All coloured cells belong to a listed run in each strip.
maths: |strips|=|clues| ∧ ∃B:set<cell>: ∃U:set<cell>: ∃O:set<cell>: B⊆C ∧ U⊆C ∧ O⊆C ∧ B∩U=∅ ∧ B∩O=∅ ∧ U∩O=∅ ∧ let colour=λc:cell: if c∈B then 1 else if c∈U then 2 else if c∈O then 3 else 0; ∀i∈[0,|strips|): ∃starts:list<position>: ∃ends:list<position>: |starts|=|clues[i]| ∧ |ends|=|clues[i]| ∧ (∀j∈[0,|clues[i]|): 0<=starts[j]<ends[j]<=|strips[i]| ∧ (∀t∈[0,|strips[i]|): starts[j]<=t ∧ t<ends[j] → colour(strips[i][t])=clues[i][j].colour) ∧ (present(clues[i][j].total) → sum_D(⟨strips[i][t]:t∈[0,|strips[i]|),starts[j]<=t ∧ t<ends[j]⟩)=unwrap(clues[i][j].total))) ∧ (∀j∈[0,|clues[i]|-1): ends[j]<=starts[j+1] ∧ (clues[i][j].colour=clues[i][j+1].colour → ends[j]<starts[j+1])) ∧ (∀t∈[0,|strips[i]|): colour(strips[i][t])!=0 ↔ ∃j∈[0,|clues[i]|): starts[j]<=t ∧ t<ends[j])
example: Satisfies a strip: blue digits [1,2], blank, blue [4] for blue clues 3,4. Breaks: blue [1,2,4] with no blank for those two blue clues. Blue [1,2] followed immediately by purple [4] is allowed for blue 3, purple 4.

name: Split pea sum

cells.description: Interior positions in traversal order, excluding every attached circle. Repeated positions retain their occurrences.

bulbs.description: The two bounding circles; either may supply the tens digit.

definition: The interior face digits total one of the two decimal numbers formed by the bounding circle digits. No distinctness condition is added.
example: Satisfies: circle digits 3 and 1 with interior 3,4,6 total 13. Breaks: the same circle digits with interior 3,4,7 total 14, neither 13 nor 31.

name: Split pea sum

cells.description: Interior positions in traversal order, excluding every attached circle. Repeated positions retain their occurrences.

bulbs.description: The two bounding circles; either may supply the tens digit.

definition: The interior face digits total one of the two decimal numbers formed by the bounding circle digits. No distinctness condition is added.
example: Satisfies: circle digits 3 and 1 with interior 3,4,6 total 13. Breaks: the same circle digits with interior 3,4,7 total 14, neither 13 nor 31.

name: Split pea

cells.description: Peach line in order, including its two green endpoint circles.

definition: Interior digits sum to the two-digit decimal number formed by the endpoint circle digits in either order.
maths: |cells|>=3 ∧ let a=D(cells[0]); let b=D(cells[|cells|-1]); let s=sum_D(betweenPositions(cells,0,|cells|-1)); s=10*a+b ∨ s=10*b+a
example: Satisfies: endpoints 1 and 2, interior [3,9] sum to 12. Breaks: endpoints 1 and 2, interior [3,8] sum to 11, neither 12 nor 21.

name: Split pea

cells.description: cells as described in the definition.

ends.description: ends as described in the definition.

definition: The cells strictly between two drawn circles sum to either decimal concatenation of the two circled face digits. End order may reverse; neither circle is in cells.
example: Satisfies: ends [3,1], cells [3,4,6], total 13. Breaks: ends [3,1], cells [3,4,7], total 14.

name: Split pea line

cells.description: Ordered path including its two circled ends.

definition: The digits strictly inside the two circles sum to a two-digit concatenation of the circled digits, in either order.
example: Satisfies: ends 1 and 3, interior 3,4,6 total 13. Breaks: same ends, interior 3,4,5 total 12.

name: Split pea line

cells.description: Ordered path including its two circled ends.

definition: The digits strictly inside the two circles sum to a two-digit concatenation of the circled digits, in either order.
example: Satisfies: ends 1 and 3, interior 3,4,6 total 13. Breaks: same ends, interior 3,4,5 total 12.

name: Split pea

cells.description: Path between successive circles, including both ends.

definition: Interior face digits sum to the two endpoint digits concatenated in either order.
maths: |cells|>=2 ∧ let a=D(cells[0]); let b=D(cells[|cells|-1]); let S=sum_D(⟨cells[i]:i∈[1,|cells|-1)⟩); S=10*a+b ∨ S=10*b+a
example: Satisfies: 3,3,4,6,1 with interior total 13. Breaks: 3,3,4,5,1 with interior total 12.

name: Exhaustive Battenburg

marks.description: Zero-based top-left positions of marked two-by-two windows.

definition: A two-by-two window is marked exactly when its diagonals have the same parity and its orthogonal neighbours have opposite parity.
example: Satisfies a marked window: rows [1,2],[4,3]. Breaks an unmarked window: the same digits form a forbidden unmarked checkerboard.
